# Every test in this workspace that is allowed to carry `#[ignore]`.
#
# Checked two ways by `ci/check-ignored-tests.ps1`: a test that starts being
# skipped and is not here is red, and a name here that no longer names a skipped
# test is red. So a change to this set is a change to this file, in the same
# commit, where somebody reads it.
#
# Generated by asking the harness, never by grepping for the attribute:
#
#     cargo test --workspace --locked -- --ignored --list
#
# Why any of them are ignored at all — the policy this list exists to state.
# Twenty-two of the twenty-four are **probes**, not regressions:
#
#   * nineteen in `bt-pty` drive real ConPTY sessions against a real PowerShell
#     and read what comes back. Their assertions are about host timing and about
#     upstream PSReadLine versions, so they answer "what does this machine do",
#     which is a question with a different right answer on every machine.
#   * two in `bt-transcript` are the reference-resolution probes over a printed
#     scrollback.
#   * one in `bt-app` writes a picture for a person to look at.
#
# A test that belongs in CI does not go on this list; it stops being ignored.
#
# **The last two are the exception, and they are on this list under protest.**
# `bt-render`'s two atlas soaks are RED gates for a user's 2026-08-29 report, not
# probes — they belong in CI and cannot be there, because CI's only adapter is
# the software one `ci/install-warp.ps1` installs. Measured on WARP on
# 2026-08-31: it holds about three bytes per rendered pixel per frame for the
# life of the process, so the first soak dies at frame 67 of 240 with the glyph
# atlas still on its first packing, before the packer either of them exists to
# examine is under any pressure. Nothing the caller does reaches it — a lower
# atlas roof, retiring each submission, and waiting the device out between frames
# were each measured and each died in the same place. On a real adapter both run
# green in about seventy seconds. Each carries the whole measurement in its own
# doc comment.
#
# So: this line of defence is currently held by whoever runs
# `cargo test -p bt-render -- --ignored` on a machine with a graphics card, and
# by nothing else. If a runner with a real adapter ever becomes available, these
# two come off this list first.
